messages:
Maya: Sandpiper-15B int8 bring-up complete. Perf vs fp16: latency down ~35%, cost down ~3.5x.
Lee: nice. any quality regressions on our summarization suite?
Maya: small one — ~2% ROUGE-L drop on long-doc summarization (docs > 6k tokens). Short docs fine.
Pranav: were you using the same max_new_tokens and batching defaults as fp16? sometimes int8 needs smaller max_new_tokens to avoid KV growth + frag.
Maya: yes — we kept max_new_tokens=512, batch_window_ms=20, batch_size cap 8. OOMs seen on a3.large-like profiles under bursty traffic (2 instances yesterday).
Jordan: can you paste the repro logs? sounds like fragmentation / slot churn rather than raw allocation.
Maya: pasted below — tail of worker log during one OOM:
```
[2024-07-08T14:12:33Z] rpc: request start model=sandpiper-15b-int8 seq_len=1024 gen=600
[2024-07-08T14:12:33Z] alloc: requested 1.2GB, free contiguous=768MB
[2024-07-08T14:12:33Z] evict: triggered KV-evict, freed 200MB
[2024-07-08T14:12:33Z] OOM: cannot satisfy allocation, aborting generation
```
Lee: KV-evict freed small chunks. pattern looks like many small allocations causing fragmentation.
Pranav: quick experiment suggestions:
- reduce max_new_tokens default to 256 for int8 on first rollout
- lower batch_window_ms to 10ms to reduce long-lived KV entries
- enable slot_compactor at low aggressiveness (compaction_threshold=0.6)
Maya: running benchmark now with those knobs. command used:
```
rbench --model sandpiper-15b-int8 --suite summarization-long --concurrency 16 --batch-cap 8 --max_new_tokens 256 --batch_window_ms 10
```
CI-bot: perf run queued -> https://ci.internal/runs/7421 (logs + token-level cost)
Maya: first pass looks promising: no OOMs in 10k requests, ROUGE-L delta now -0.6% (was -2%). latency p95 increased ~3% vs earlier int8 run but still below fp16.
Jordan: small latency hit acceptable if we avoid OOMs; need to track unit-cost. can we try selective KV-eviction policy: evict-only-prefixes > 1024 tokens and keep short sessions cached?
Pranav: yep — I'll prototype a policy and add a canary config: kv.evict_min_prefix=1024, kv.eviction_stride=128.
Maya: plan: roll canary with max_new_tokens=256 + batch_window_ms=10 + slot_compactor=0.6 on 10% of traffic for 48h. monitor: ROUGE, p95, OOM rate, cost/token.
Lee: add automatic rollback trigger if OOMs > 0.05% or ROUGE drop > 1%.
Jordan: I'll own the runbook for rolling back and notify infra if we see host-level OOMs.
Maya: thanks — creating canary now. will post CI link + metrics in this thread later. :thumbsup:
CI-bot: Canary deployment started: canary-id=canary-2024-07-08-09, targets=10% traffic.
Maya: (update) after 12h canary: OOMs=0, ROUGE-L delta -0.4%, p95 down 28% vs fp16, cost/token -3.2x. we should be good for gradual rollout.
Lee: excellent. follow-up: add a short eval to onboarding checklist -> "int8: recommend default max_new_tokens=256, batch_window_ms<=10, enable slot_compactor".
Pranav: I'll add that to model-config templates and push a doc with rationale + tuning knobs.
Jordan: tagging SRE to watch host-level swap churn during ramp. @SRE-team FYI.
Maya: closing loop, thanks all.
